land.text: the country east of the Tarum (Citarum) River

predecessors.note: Galuh was 'established as a breakaway kingdom' of Tarumanagara around 669; Wretikandayun founded it in 612 within Tarumanagara (Tarumanagara page), after Manikmaya's Kendan near Nagreg (526).

land.text: Galuh, the eastern half of the Sunda-Galuh realm

successors.note: 'Unification of Sunda and Galuh: 1482'. A new Galuh polity centred at Panaekan emerged in the 16th century and was conquered by Mataram in 1595 (Galuh page); it is not this state.

capitals.name: Karangkamulyan (Bojong Galuh)
capitals.note: The page has the capital at Bojong Galuh (Karangkamulyan) in the 6th century, then Saunggalah (Kuningan) without dates, then Kawali; the end year 1199 only means 'by the 13th century'.

capitals.name: Kawali (Ciamis)
capitals.note: '13th century: the capital had shifted to Kawali'; the Astana Gede inscription at Kawali (14th century) is the kingdom's only stone inscription.

rulers.name: Bratasena
rulers.note: Fled after Purbasora's invasion; father of Sanjaya.

rulers.name: Purbasora
rulers.note: Invaded Galuh in 716 with Indraprasta; killed in 723.

rulers.name: Tamperan Barmawijaya
rulers.note: Son of Sanjaya; killed by Manarah in 739.

rulers.name: Manarah
rulers.note: Subject of the Ciung Wanara folktale.

rulers.name: Guruminda Sang Minisri
rulers.note: The table lists no later kings.

correction.text: Galuh, east of the Citarum: Cliopatria's 674 shape held from 612, as Tarumanagara's dependent until 670

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Galuh row starts 674, but the Tarumanagara page has 'In 612, his grandson Wretikandayun founded the Galuh Kingdom' and the Galuh page's table has him reigning 612-702; the Galuh page's infobox dates the separation from Tarumanagara to 669 (text: 670). The shape is Cliopatria's 674 shape unchanged; no page gives the extent of Wretikandayun's realm.

36,212 km2 for 674-723. The page describes the territory as 'running from the Citarum River in the west to the Cipamali and Cisarayu rivers in the east'; the shape runs 106.9-110.1E, a little beyond those rivers. No infobox area.

correction.text: Galuh restored under Manarah: Cliopatria's 741 shape held from 739

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 739-740, which Cliopatria leaves empty: Tamperan Barmawijaya (732-739) was 'killed by Manarah in 739', and Manarah reigns 739-783, so Galuh is its own kingdom again two years before Cliopatria's 741 row. The shape is the 741 shape unchanged.
35,841 km2 for 741-824: the same Citarum-to-Cipamali land under Manarah (739-783) and Guruminda (783-799).

unverified: page budget. 35,841 km2 for 896-1009, after Cliopatria's gap 825-895 (Galuh inside Sunda). The Galuh page's king list stops at 799 and says Galuh was absorbed into Sunda in the 10th century (approximate), which sits badly with a separate Galuh shape until 1027.
unverified: page budget. 36,212 km2 for 1010-1027, 371 km2 more than 896; no page explains the sliver.

35,841 km2 for 1475-1481: the Sunda page's table: Niskala Wastu Kancana 'split Sunda and Galuh between his two sons'; 'Ningrat Kancana (Galuh), 1475-1482'; the 'Twin equal kingdom of Sunda and Galuh'.

region.text: Galuh, the country east of the Citarum

ledger.note: 612: Wretikandayun founds Galuh. 'In 612, his grandson Wretikandayun founded the Galuh Kingdom' (Manikmaya had founded Kendan near Nagreg in 526); the Galuh page's table has him reigning 612-702. Galuh is Tarumanagara's dependent until 670; no page gives the land of 612 (the 674 shape is the reading).

region.text: the Galuh Kingdom (east), east of the Tarum (Citarum) River

ledger.note: 669: Galuh stands alone. Infobox 'Separation from Tarumanagara by Wretikandayun: 669 AD'; the text has 'In 670, Tarumanagara was divided into the Sunda Kingdom (west) and the Galuh Kingdom (east), separated by the Tarum (Citarum) River'.

region.text: Galuh, the country east of the Citarum

ledger.note: 723: Sanjaya's invasion ends Galuh's independence. Purbasora (716-723) was 'killed in 723' during the invasion; Premanadikusuma was 'appointed by Sanjaya' (723-732); Galuh 'came under Mataram influence'. The page does not describe the campaign, and the Sanjaya page (thin) has only the Carita Parahyangan portrayal of him as 'the Sundanese king and hero of Galuh'.

region.text: Galuh, the country east of the Citarum

ledger.note: 739: Manarah takes Galuh back from Sanjaya's line. Tamperan Barmawijaya (732-739), Sanjaya's son, was 'killed by Manarah in 739'; Manarah reigns 739-783. Cliopatria's Galuh row resumes in 741.

region.text: Galuh, the country east of the Citarum

ledger.note: c. 825: Galuh drops out of Cliopatria and sits inside Sunda until 895 (the year is Cliopatria's; the pages opened are silent on 825). The Galuh page has Galuh 'absorbed into the Sunda kingdom' in the 10th century (approximate).

region.text: Galuh, the country east of the Citarum

ledger.note: c. 896: Galuh stands apart from Sunda again (Cliopatria's year; page silent).

region.text: Galuh, the country east of the Citarum

ledger.note: c. 1028: Galuh is joined to Sunda until 1474 (Cliopatria's year; page silent). The page: 'the two later formed the United Kingdom of Sunda and Galuh'.
13th century: the court is at Kawali. 'the capital had shifted to Kawali' by the 13th century; the year 1200 only stands for that century.
1475: Galuh is a separate kingdom again. The Sunda page's table: Niskala Wastu Kancana 'split Sunda and Galuh between his two sons'; 'Ningrat Kancana (Galuh), 1475-1482'.
1482: Galuh is united with Sunda. 'Unification of Sunda and Galuh: 1482' (infobox); Jayadewata rules both from Pakuan (Sunda page). The Galuh page gives no dissolution as such.

wars.name: Sanjaya's invasion of Galuh
wars.outcome: Purbasora is killed in 723 and Sanjaya's appointee Premanadikusuma takes the throne; Galuh 'came under Mataram influence' until 739.
wars.note: Purbasora had himself invaded Galuh in 716 with Indraprasta, driving out Bratasena, Sanjaya's father. The page does not describe the campaign.

wars.name: Manarah's revolt against Tamperan
wars.outcome: Tamperan Barmawijaya, Sanjaya's son, is killed by Manarah in 739; Galuh is Manarah's until 783.
wars.note: The Ciung Wanara folktale; the page gives only the reign table.

certainty.note: The page gives river lines (Citarum, Cipamali, Cisarayu) and no surveyed frontier.

notes: Start 612 (Wretikandayun, Tarumanagara page and the Galuh page's reign table) against the Galuh infobox 'Separation from Tarumanagara: 669' and its text 670: Galuh is read as a kingdom within Tarumanagara's sphere from 612 and sovereign from 670; the Tarumanagara dossier carries the vassal_start/vassal_end pair for 612-670. Cliopatria's Galuh row (674-1481) is one state with gaps 724-740, 825-895 and 1028-1474, where the Sunda row absorbs it; those gaps are carried as ledger loss/gain events (723 and 739 are dated by the Galuh page; 825, 896 and 1028 are Cliopatria's years, 'unverified: page budget'). The Galuh page says Galuh was absorbed into Sunda in the 10th century and ends its king list at 799, so the real union may be much earlier than 1028 or the separate Galuh of 896-1027 spurious. End 1482 (infobox 'Unification of Sunda and Galuh: 1482'), Cliopatria's last shape ends 1481. The 16th-century Galuh at Panaekan (conquered by Mataram in 1595) is a different, later polity and is not covered. Infobox gives no area. Gazetteer names wanted: places Karangkamulyan, Kawali, Kuningan, Ciamis; rivers Citarum, Cipamali, Cisarayu.
